source: Field-tested question bank of the `req` plugin (aeon). Every OFFICIAL question here earned its place by surfacing a forgotten rule in real client work. Do NOT add questions derived from theory. Tier 1 ships PROVISIONAL on purpose — see tiers.1.status. Design notes: docs/requirement/req-skill-design.md §4.

1.pipeline_steps: 1-4 — End Goal · Scope · Actors · Ubiquitous Language
1.when: once per module, after /req:capture, before the first rule question
1.round_map: 6 questions in `order`, taken 3 at a time: round A = end_goal + scope x2 (what counts as done, and how far) · round B = actors x2 + language (who, and what things are called). per_round stays 3 — ask_rules is untouched.
1.requires: spec.sources[] must not be empty. A framing red card has to point somewhere, and the schema allows `question.raised_by` to be a SRC-xxx or a BR-xxx@vN only (check #4 resolves it). Tier 1 runs before any rule exists, so SRC is the only option left. No source -> say so and stop; run /req:capture first.
1.star_rule: The star on a TIER 1 question is NOT the owner's habit. It is the reading taken from the captured input, and it must be shown with its SRC id and locator next to it. Habits repeat across projects; an end goal does not. If the input supports no option, ask with no star and say the input is silent. (Tier 2 keeps owner_pattern below.)
1.may_not_write_why: Framing is pipeline steps 1-4; rules start at step 5. An answer that states a rule is reported at the stop and drafted by its tier 2 category, with provenance pointing back at the same source. deferred_questions[] is closed to tier 1 by the SCHEMA, not by preference: deferredQuestion.category is an enum of the ten tier 2 categories only.
1.coverage: session-tracked, same as tier 2. Readable hints only, never a gate: REQ.goal / REQ.actor filled (check #1 already errors when they are not), REQ.business_value filled, glossary[] non-empty (check #11, warn). `scope` has nothing to read — see declared_gap.
1.declared_gap: There is no queryable out-of-scope field in spec.json. In-scope shows up as which REQ exist; an exclusion lands in requirements[].narrative and in the round report; a disputed exclusion becomes a Q-xxx red card. Adding meta.out_of_scope[] would touch meta (additionalProperties:false), both fixtures, possibly rollup + check #9, the renderer and EXPECTED.md — that is a round of its own, not a side effect of this one.
1.promotion: A tier 1 question becomes official when it has surfaced a rule someone had forgotten on REAL CLIENT WORK at least once: record where in `field_evidence` and drop `status`. `derived_from` is where the wording came from, never evidence — teaching material and a fictional teaching project cannot promote a question. Until then the whole tier stays provisional (design §4: สร้างเป็นร่างก่อน แล้วเลื่อนเป็นทางการหลังใช้จริงรอบแรก).

2.pipeline_steps: 5-7 — Business Rules · Calculation Contract · State Machine
2.when: every round, per requirement, repeatable until the relevant categories are covered

ask_rules.note: The starred default is the OWNER'S DESIGN HABIT, not a domain law. Pre-select it, never skip the asking. Enterprise work often wants the opposite (retry queues, effective dates). Tier 1 stars mean something different — see tiers.1.star_rule.

owner_pattern: Consistently picks simple / direct / fail-loudly (round everywhere, fail fast, hit the constraint, see only your own) over clever / flexible / swallow-the-error. Recorded from tier 2 rounds only.

questions.why_this_shape: Asked as a pair, not as "define your terms": people can always define a word, and cannot always say whether two words are the same thing. The pair is what tells you a class is about to be duplicated.
questions.repeat: This is the one tier 1 question worth firing more than once in a session — once per colliding pair the input contains. It still counts as one of the three in its round; extra pairs go to the next round.
